zh: 但我确实认为，对于普通消费者来说，助手在你最忙碌的时候最有帮助，对吧？

en: It's most helpful when you're gardening or cooking or doing things where your hands are busy and you can't actually engage with an interface.

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, it goes back to that like invisible assistant where you can just talk and say something and it just goes and runs and does something in the background.
zh: 而且，你知道，这又回到了那种隐形助手的场景，你只需要开口说点什么，它就会在后台跑起来去做事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that the...
zh: 而且我认为……

speaker: Unknown
en: Tech bubble that is chronically online and on their phone and in front of a computer is a very different environment than the general population.
zh: 那些长期泡在网上、盯着手机、坐在电脑前的科技圈人群，和普通人群所处的是一个非常不同的环境。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I'm really excited to see how does this actually hit mass adoption and how does like the average consumer think about an assistant when it's actually like, is it going to be an assistant that solves real pain points for them where they're going to use it when something is really, really painful because they don't want to do it?
zh: 所以我非常期待看到这个东西到底如何实现大规模普及，以及普通消费者会怎么看待一个助手，实际上就是，它会成为一个为他们解决真实痛点的助手吗？他们会在事情真的非常非常痛苦的时候去用它，因为他们不想自己去做那件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: Like you get a traffic ticket, you have to go pay for that traffic ticket.
zh: 比如你吃了一张交通罚单，你必须去缴纳那张罚单。

speaker: Unknown
en: Great.
zh: 好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just take a picture and let your agent go do it for you.
zh: 拍张照，然后让你的智能体替你去办。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's gonna be interesting to see.
zh: 这会很值得观察。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the next thing I wanted to talk to you about was social.
zh: 所以我接下来想和你聊的是社交。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we talked in multiplayer generally.
zh: 你知道，我们大体上聊过多人的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we talked about how iMessage is this sort of privileged place to be, which is actually one of the cool things about Instinct.
zh: 你知道，我们聊过 iMessage 是一个多么有特权的位置，这实际上也是 Instinct 的一个很酷的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, in my experience, building agents that you add to group chats somehow feels intrusive or like it diminishes social capital.
zh: 然而，根据我的经验，把智能体加到群聊里，不知怎么总感觉有点侵入性，或者说它削减了社交资本。

speaker: Unknown
en: Super.
zh: 太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you seen anything that works well?
zh: 你有没有见过什么做得好的案例？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what are your kind of theories for how these agents get to a multiplayer state?
zh: 对于这些智能体如何达到多人状态，你有什么样的理论？

speaker: Unknown
en: A lot of people have tried it.
zh: 很多人都尝试过。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think I've seen three different approaches.
zh: 我见过三种不同的做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: The first approach is your traditional added to a group chat and it's just like the group chat and your companion.
zh: 第一种做法是传统的被加到群聊里，它就像群聊和你的伙伴一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second approach I've seen is how instinct did it, where you have like an agent network where you invite another agent and they're talking behind the scenes on your behalf and they'll update you as to what's going on.
zh: 我见过的第二种做法是 Instinct 的做法，就是你有一个智能体网络，你邀请另一个智能体，它们在幕后代表你交流，并且会向你更新情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third way that I've seen it, which I think is the most interesting, it's a new one called Doc by this guy Shane Mack.
zh: 我见过的第三种方式，我觉得是最有意思的，是一个叫 Doc 的新产品，出自一个叫 Shane Mack 的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think also an A16Z company.
zh: 我记得也是一家 A16Z 的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: XMTP.
zh: XMTP。

speaker: Unknown
en: And they are approaching it more like granola.
zh: 而他们的做法更像是 granola。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you add an agent to a group chat, but that agent is silent and it's purely a listener.
zh: 所以你把一个智能体加到群聊里，但那个智能体是沉默的，纯粹是一个倾听者。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's taking notes on what people are talking about.
zh: 它在记录人们谈论的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it has an action item, it independently will ping the person in a separate message thread.
zh: 而如果它有一个行动项,它会独立地在单独的消息线程里去提醒那个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then if you want to see what people are talking about, you can go into the actual docs and see what it's taken notes on.
zh: 然后如果你想看看人们在聊什么,你可以进入实际的文档,看它做了哪些笔记。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that way it's more of, again, it's your invisible agent.
zh: 这样一来,它更像是——再说一次——它是你的隐形智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't know it's there.
zh: 你不知道它在那里。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's doing all the admin work that you would want out of a multiplayer function.
zh: 它在做你希望多人协作功能做的所有行政工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if it needs action items, it doesn't bother the majority of the group.
zh: 而如果它需要行动项,它不会打扰群里的大多数人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Really, really cool approach.
zh: 真的、真的很棒的思路。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got to try that out.
zh: 我得去试试。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that.
zh: 我喜欢这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: I love that it's an A16Z company already, of course.
zh: 我喜欢它已经是 A16Z 的投资公司了,当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: Of course.
zh: 当然。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, my theory on this, if you look at this, and Nir from Obo said it, and I think he's right, which is the progress the models are making on verifiable domains like coding are, of course, exponential, but the progress they've made on just prose quality and even like bedside manner has maybe plateaued or maybe is even getting worse.
zh: 你知道,我对此的理论是,如果你看这个,Nir from Obo 说过,我认为他是对的,那就是模型在像编码这类可验证领域取得的进展当然是指数级的,但它们在纯粹的文章质量、甚至 bedside manner 方面取得的进展可能已经趋于平缓,甚至可能在变差。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually think that with the models as they are today, and perhaps with our own expectations in terms of these social dynamics, I don't think there's a lot of ways that the agents can contribute and enhance the sort of social connectivity of the group.
zh: 所以我实际上认为,以今天的模型,以及也许以我们自己对这些社交动态的期望来说,我不认为智能体有很多方式可以贡献和增强群体的社交连接性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, conversely, I think agents that are very utilitarian, you know, one of the experiments I've been doing is adding it, I'm a collector, you know, I collect records and a bunch of other things, adding an agent to the chats where I talk to my fellow collector friends and trying to catalog our respective collections and our tastes.
zh: 你知道,反过来说,我认为非常实用主义的智能体——我做的一个实验是,我是一个收藏者,我收集唱片和一堆其他东西——把它加进我和收藏同好们聊天的群聊里,试图给我们的各自收藏和品味做编目。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I haven't quite hit it, but it at least feels like it's something that's genuinely additive to the group rather than, you know, this sort of low EQ robot that's chattering when we don't want it to.
zh: 我还没完全做到,但至少感觉它是对群体真正有增益的东西,而不是那种我们不想要它说话时却喋喋不休的低情商机器人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep, totally.
zh: 是的,完全。

speaker: Unknown
en: You should give Doc a try.
zh: 你应该试试 Doc。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think you're gonna be quite fascinated by it.
zh: 我觉得你会非常着迷的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I will, yeah.
zh: 我会的,好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, the other interesting take that I heard this week was that something about messaging in particular doesn't lend itself to these agent interactions because in messaging, it's as if somebody has the mic and it feels uncomfortable to give the agent the mic.
zh: 是的,我这周听到的另一个有意思的观点是,消息传递这个场景有某种特殊性,不太适合这些智能体交互,因为在消息里,就好像某个人拿着麦克风,而把麦克风交给智能体会让人感觉不舒服。

speaker: Unknown
en: Whereas if you look at something like maybe closer to a Discord or even a traditional web form,
zh: 而如果你看更接近 Discord 甚至传统网页论坛的东西,

speaker: Unknown
en: That's actually something where an agent can make a post and you can either engage with the post or not, Reddit style, but for some reason it feels less intrusive than group chat.
zh: 那其实是智能体可以发帖的场景,你可以参与这个帖子也可以不参与,Reddit 风格,但不知为何感觉比群聊的侵入性要小。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know.
zh: 我不确定。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, interesting.
zh: 是的,有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's almost as if we're trying to humanize these agents a little too much.
zh: 这几乎就像是我们在把这些智能体人性化了那么一点点过头了。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's right.
zh: 没错。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that comes to another component where if you look at the actual design of the character of the agent, I see some companies that have it try to be like an AI-generated human.
zh: 而我认为这引出了另一个方面,如果你看智能体这个角色的实际设计,我看到一些公司让它试图像一个 AI 生成的人类。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you have other companies like Muse that it's this like adorable Yeti.
zh: 然后你有其他公司,像 Muse,它是这只可爱的雪人。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think it's really interesting to see how the world has fallen in love with this Yeti.
zh: 而且我认为非常有意思的是看到全世界都爱上了这只雪人。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just so cute and adorable.
zh: 它就是那么可爱、那么讨人喜欢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the like AI-generated human
zh: 而那种 AI 生成的人类

speaker: Unknown
en: To your point, I think people feel a little uncomfortable.
zh: 正如你所说,我觉得人们会觉得有点不舒服。

speaker: Unknown
en: It feels weird to humanize these assistants so much in your personal space.
zh: 在你的个人空间里把这些助手如此人性化感觉挺怪的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one related question I wanted to ask you is, do you think that the market segments by personality or archetype, you know, we were chatting a bit about this in our walk, but, you know, some people prefer a kind of serious, gruff, authoritative doctor, and some people prefer a, you know, warm and friendly, you know, sort of a doctor that feels like a peer.
zh: 所以我想问你一个相关的问题是,你认为市场会按个性或原型来细分吗,你知道,我们在散步时聊了一点这个,但是,你知道,有些人喜欢一种严肃、粗鲁、有权威感的医生,有些人喜欢一种温暖友好的、你知道,那种感觉像同伴的医生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And those are just two different archetypes of doctors.
zh: 而这些只是医生的两种不同原型。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, no doctor is both of those things.
zh: 显然,没有哪个医生能同时是这两种。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're in opposition.
zh: 它们是对立的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Do you think the same will be true of agents?
zh: 你认为智能体也会是这样吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: I think everyone for sure prefers a different style of communication.
zh: 我认为每个人肯定偏好不同的沟通风格。

speaker: Unknown
en: Poke came out of the gates hot, right?
zh: Poke 一出场就很火爆,对吧?

speaker: Unknown

zh: Poke 的个性相当鲜明,我有很多朋友说,我拒绝把我任何个人信息给 poke,因为它太嘴贱了,和它对话实际上让我感到不舒服。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I don't think personality is really a defensible moat because it's quite easy to configure.
zh: 但我不认为个性真的是一条可防御的护城河,因为它很容易配置。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's like you as a consumer, you text your agent, you say that you would prefer it responds in a certain way.
zh: 就像你作为消费者,你给你的智能体发消息,说你不希望它以某种方式回应。

speaker: Unknown
en: It just saves that to its memory or its sole file and then you're good to go and it changes.
zh: 它只是把那个保存到它的记忆或它的 sole 文件里,然后你就可以继续了,它就改变了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we'll get to a place where whatever general agent ends up being the leader that it'll be quite configurable and each person can kind of tailor the agent to speak to them how, you know, however makes them most comfortable.
zh: 我认为我们会到达一个阶段,无论哪个通用智能体最终成为领先者,它都会是相当可配置的,每个人都可以量身定制智能体对自己说话的方式,你知道,以任何让他们最舒适的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's interesting, and I agree with you, but maybe let me try the steel man here for not just personality, but kind of, you know, constitution, for lack of a better word, which is an example of a kind of defining characteristic is presumptuousness.
zh: 这很有意思,我同意你,但也许让我尝试为——不只是个性,而是某种,你知道,宪法,找不到更好的词——做一个最强辩护,其中一个定义性特征的例子是擅自假定性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, we've talked a little bit about this, and there are some jobs for which you want the agent to be highly presumptuous.
zh: 你知道,我们稍微聊过这个,有些工作你确实希望智能体高度擅自假定。

speaker: Unknown
en: And you'd rather have it make mistakes 10% of the time as long as it often gets things done.
zh: 而你宁愿它有 10% 的时间犯错，只要它经常把事情办成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are other styles of agents, like our finance agent perhaps, where you want it to be highly cautious.
zh: 还有其他风格的智能体，比如我们的金融智能体，你可能希望它高度谨慎。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I sort of wonder if some of these things, which we're now describing as personality, start to push down into sort of capabilities and how it tie-breaks in a position of ambiguity.
zh: 所以我有点好奇，这些我们现在描述为「个性」的东西，是否开始下沉为某种能力，以及它在模糊情境下如何做取舍。

speaker: Unknown
en: And perhaps there's a bit more defensibility around that.
zh: 也许在这方面会有更多的可防御性。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there is massive defensibility around proactivity.
zh: 我认为在主动性方面存在巨大的可防御性。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think that's actually going to be something that separates the winner from the meat of the pack.
zh: 我觉得这实际上会是把赢家与一大群平庸者区分开来的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The agent that can be most proactive, that can serve as an invisible assistant and start doing things on your behalf without you even asking.
zh: 最具主动性的智能体，能够充当隐形助手，在你甚至没有开口的情况下就开始替你做事。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the best like gimmick, cool, aha moment that we've seen so far is checking into your flight for you.
zh: 我觉得到目前为止我们见过的最棒的、最酷的、最有「啊哈」时刻的花招，就是帮你值机。

speaker: Unknown
en: To your point though, it really does come down to two categories.
zh: 不过正如你所说，这确实归结为两类。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's some workflows where
zh: 有一些工作流程，

speaker: Unknown
en: You want to retain control and you don't really want an agent to be acting too proactive on your behalf.
zh: 你想保留控制权，你并不真的希望智能体太主动地替你行事。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think those are workflows that require a change in action on your side.
zh: 而我认为那些是需要你这边做出行动变更的工作流程。

speaker: Unknown
en: So maybe that is...
zh: 所以也许那是……

speaker: Unknown
en: An agent identifies that the insurance you're using is charging too much money and thinks you should switch insurances.
zh: 一个智能体发现你正在使用的保险收费太高，认为你应该换保险。

speaker: Unknown
en: It should probably get your permission before it actually makes that switch because that's a direct action on your behalf that impacts you.
zh: 它在实际做出更换之前应该先征得你的许可，因为那是直接影响你的、以你名义进行的直接行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: However, the proactiveness of, hey, I drafted this email for you or I got a flight credit on your behalf.
zh: 然而，像「嘿，我帮你起草好了这封邮件」或者「我帮你拿到了航班积分」这种主动性，

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no action needed on your side.
zh: 你这边不需要任何行动。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's just saving you money.
zh: 它只是在帮你省钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's saving you time.
zh: 它在帮你省时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think it'll be interesting to see how do we really categorize and break down those type of behaviors.
zh: 所以我觉得有趣的是，我们如何真正对这类行为进行分类和拆解。

speaker: Unknown
en: But it will be a very fine line because if you cross that line once, I think you immediately lose all trust with your user.
zh: 但这会是一条非常细微的界线，因为一旦你跨过那条线，我想你会立刻失去用户的所有信任。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it'll be interesting.
zh: 是的，这会很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were joking internally, like we're days away from an agent messaging someone saying, I noticed you weren't that into her, so I went ahead and broke up with her for you.
zh: 我们内部还在开玩笑说，距离某个智能体给某人发消息说「我注意到你对她没那么上心，所以我已经替你和她分手了」，只有几天之遥了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yep.
zh: 对。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, so like- Saw that one.
zh: 你知道的，就像—— 见过那条了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's going to happen, man.
zh: 这事会发生的，兄弟。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, I think a lot of the magic comes from the presumptuousness.
zh: 但你知道，我觉得很多魔力正是来自那种自作主张。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that if you didn't see people posting on X about, oh, the agent did this, the agent did that, it would probably be a sign that the agents are not pushing hard enough in this direction.
zh: 而且我觉得，如果你没看到有人在 X 上发帖说「哦，这个智能体做了这个，那个智能体做了那个」，那大概说明智能体们在这个方向上推得还不够狠。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, I'd be curious to know, first of all, I'm a little suspicious of whether the bong chang
zh: 实际上，我很好奇想知道，首先，我有点怀疑那个 bong chang

speaker: Unknown
en: That post was even real.
zh: 那条帖子到底是不是真的。

zh: 给不了解情况的朋友说一下，有个人发推说 Instinct 帮他值了机，把他的中间名幻听成了 Bong Chang，导致他没能登上航班。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm not sure if that's just shitposting or if that really happened.
zh: 所以我不确定那只是在 shitposting 还是真有其事。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I'd be curious to know if that person is still using Instinct.
zh: 但我很好奇想知道那个人是否还在用 Instinct。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm guessing they are.
zh: 我猜他们在用。

speaker: Unknown
en: I would assume so, purely given the traction of that post.
zh: 我会这么假设，纯粹从那条帖子的热度来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're probably beating for more content there.
zh: 他们大概还在为更多内容而拼搏。

speaker: Unknown
en: I see.
